Steps advance only on executed comparable work without an adverse signal; nothing progresses from elapsed calendar time alone; completed history and official plan state stay immutable.

Week-1 planned running minutes (walks excluded; walk/jog counts its jogging minutes) <= current reported or wearable-conservative weekly running minutes; when current exposure is zero or unknown, or the athlete is a novice, only the listed establishment entries (walk/jog ladder step 0, the 15-20 minute easy entry) are used.
Week-1 long run <= the longest current run reported; rounding may not exceed it.
No quality, strides or race-effort work in week 1 except a current familiar quality task that fits inside the week-1 running ceiling.
Unknowns are emitted with one of the four categories; ASK only for facts that change the first program (eligibility, goal, chosen days and session time, event date); clinical flags route to a human.
A restart-after-pause class requires R6-NONCLINICAL-RETURN authority and a pause reason that passes the clinical-reason check of that boundary.
Load-establishment rows appear only when R6-LOAD-ESTABLISHMENT is enabled.
Sex, height and weight never enter dose; an event time goal never sets pace.
An intake pause needs a structured nonclinical reason category; free text alone is ASK and can only add CLINICAL or ASK outcomes.

A non-novice whose longest current run or weekly running is below run.minimumSessionMinutes starts on the walk/jog ladder at the highest step whose jogging per session is <= the longest current run and <= current weekly running divided by the walk/jog exposures of the week; no week-1 session holds more running than the longest current run (D42).

Intake loads: a pound value converts to kilograms at the nearest 0.5 kg and keeps the reported value; any other or missing unit leaves the load unknown and asked; a reported known dose above six sets starts at six.

An eligibility flag that means yes in any form (true, 1, yes, y, sim, si or sí, trimmed, in any letter case and with or without accents) routes CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED; any other non-boolean flag leaves eligibility unassessed (ASK), never clearance and never assumed illness.
limitations: Onboarding facts are self-report; wearable history may be partial.
No evidence validates the exact starter doses or establishment length.
Profiles outside V1 (elite, adolescent, pregnancy/postpartum, clinical) are excluded, not evaluated.

The interruption-reason text screen is a lexicon heuristic; any further lexical residual is an owned open gap, and the structured category plus current eligibility (dated after the break, every clinical flag false) remain the primary defence.
The familiar start rests on self-reported longest and weekly running; equivalence of intermittent and continuous jogging is unstudied.

Steps advance only on executed comparable work without an adverse signal; nothing progresses from elapsed calendar time alone; completed history and official plan state stay immutable.
Athletes with strength class NONE complete unloaded or light-implement practice before any effort-guided loaded set; the first loaded exposure is at most 2 sets at RIR >= 3.

The establishment instruction describes an ascending ramp: start with the lightest available load and add the smallest increment between preparatory sets while at least the target reserve remains with stable technique; the working load is the heaviest such load; load and convention are recorded.
No kilogram is derived from sex, body mass, another exercise or implement; a stale or differently configured known load is only a hint or ceiling.

After establishment, a load or repetition step requires a logged set record meeting target repetitions with reserve >= prescribed RIR - 1; otherwise the dose holds. A logged load above the planned load is adopted only when that exposure meets this criterion and only up to one smallest increment above the plan, never above a re-establishment ceiling; otherwise the planned load stays the reference and the logged load is asked about. A logged load at or below the plan is executed evidence; a changed known load is a modification (D44).
RIR is treated as approximate (about one repetition of error); technique and comfort govern continuation and stopping.
Fail-closed: no ESTABLISH rows are emitted when this boundary is not enabled.

A load logged on an establishment row becomes a prescribed numeric (KNOWN) load only after the athlete confirms it (in kilograms or pounds, in the planned convention), after a second logged exposure of the exercise in a separate session (later, or earlier in the same week) within establishmentAgreementIncrements smallest increment of it, or when it lies within one smallest increment of the athlete's own load hint in the same convention. Until then the next exposure is FROM_LOG with no number, its instructions describe effort-guided selection only and never point to the logged value (D48), and the logged value is asked about. Numeric plausibility of a confirmed or repeated value is Data-owned (D45).

Loads are kilograms in the engine: a pound value (intake or log) converts at the nearest 0.5 kg and keeps the reported value; another or missing unit, or a logged convention different from the planned one, is never adopted and is asked about; no prescription carries pounds or a known load above 500 kg.

An above-plan logged load is adopted only when that exercise's gate for the week is ADVANCE or EARNED; a missing reps-in-reserve log, an adverse response or a converging-fatigue hold keeps the planned load and the load is asked about (D44).

Establishment needs an executed exposure: an establishment exposure that was missed, or dated inside a declared pause, establishes nothing, so the next exposure is again the effort-guided establishment row (at most 2 sets at RIR >= 3, the ramp-up, no load, no progression step); a FROM_LOG row exists only for an exercise with a logged load (pending or adopted) and never says 'use the load you logged' without one (D52).

An exercise not performed for more than return.moderateMaxDays, counted in calendar days from its last executed exposure (completed-work ledger), restarts with effort-guided establishment with its last logged load as a ceiling and regains its earlier set count one set per executed week, whether the absence came from rotation, a substitution window, skipped sessions or a return (strength.resumeAfterDays; D52).
limitations: Evidence for RIR accuracy in never-trained adults is thin.
Self-selected loads by novices tend to be conservative; early weeks may under-dose.
Self-selected load evidence is abstract-level; plausibility rules for logged values are Data-owned.
The agreement tolerance is a data-consistency rule; plausibility of repeated or confirmed values is Data-owned and not yet defined.
D52 was found in round 10 and predates FREEZE-1; until it is fixed, a missed first exposure or weeks of skipped strength sessions bypass establishment.

Operational values are reversible coaching choices inside the envelope, never physiological thresholds, injury-prevention rules, readiness scores, finish-time promises or individual-response predictions.
Steps advance only on executed comparable work without an adverse signal; nothing progresses from elapsed calendar time alone; completed history and official plan state stay immutable.

One progression dimension per session type per week; EARNED may release a step the cadence would otherwise hold or skip a consolidation hold, but never adds more than one step on any dimension in a week, and is unavailable in WALK_JOG, RESTART and RETURN modes.

Every step requires executed comparable sessions without an adverse signal in the gating week; quality/strides activation, block-boundary set increases and ladder steps count executed weeks, never calendar weeks.

Single-run ceiling (operational.run.singleRunCeiling): no planned run other than the race exceeds the longest completed run of the preceding 30 days (completed-work ledger, the intake-reported longest current run while within 30 days of intake, a valid return demonstration) by more than one stepMinutes; walk/jog ladder sessions and walks follow the ladder, whose start never holds more jogging per session than the longest current run (D42); with nothing completed in the window the reviewed entry (return.entryRunMinutes) is the ceiling in every week, not only the first.

When the 30-day reference run is under 50 minutes, the 5-minute step exceeds 10% of it; the step stays response-gated, is disclosed, and is never combined with another single-session increase in the same week. A long-run step that the long-run share cap holds is not a single-session increase: that week the easy step and the quality step proceed under their own gates and cadence, and if either steps the long-run target waits where it was prescribed. In such a week the stepped easy run may equal the long run prescribed that week, never exceed it. A long run held at the single-run ceiling is still a step beyond the 30-day reference (D50, resolved in round 10).

Strength ADVANCE requires logged target repetitions and minimum logged RIR >= prescribed RIR - 1; EARNED requires minimum logged RIR >= prescribed RIR + 2 on two comparable exposures outside consolidation; a known-load or bodyweight repetition or load step requires a logged set for that exercise in the gating week; missing logs or unknown logged RIR hold the dose without regression; a logged load above the plan never becomes the reference unless that exposure met the ADVANCE criterion (D44).

longRunShareOfWeeklyMinutesMax limits long-run growth in weeks with at least three running sessions; the cap holds the long run and never shortens it below the typical easy run or the last build week's long run; consolidation, taper and return reductions are separate rules.
Transition magnitudes (restart step and switch point, walk/jog exit dose, consolidation reduction, post-event redevelopment) are declared in the policy, not hard-coded.
Repeated adverse responses (two comparable within 14 days at the current dose after any regression) regress one step; a single adverse response holds.

A run dimension or exercise with no executed session in the reviewed week holds: it never counts as an executed week, never advances a walk/jog step, never unlocks quality or strides and never converts a walk. In a conditional projection a week with no planned session of a dimension likewise never counts as executed for it (D46).
After an exercise is re-established by effort, its earlier set count returns at most one set per executed week.

Return-entry and return-step exposures never count toward a block-boundary set increase: a development block with any such exposure of the exercise earns no set, including the block in progress at the break. After the return steps the set count comes back at most one set per executed week without a phase reduction, up to the ceiling (the last set count executed before the break outside a phase reduction), with phase reductions on top; it goes above the ceiling only through a later development block with no return-step exposure (operational.return.strengthReturnSets; D49, shared with R6-NONCLINICAL-RETURN).

With no easy run planned in a week (every easy day a walk), the executed long run gates the development-week count and the walk-to-run conversion; a converted walk becomes an easy run at run.minimumSessionMinutes that then progresses like the others (R12). In a conditional projection, restart and return sessions of any role gate on EASY, as in reviews (R13).
limitations: Step sizes, cadence and consolidation are operational, not evidence-derived optima.
Single-session injury association is observational and distance-based.
Strength progression evidence is from trained lifters over 8 weeks.

In consolidation weeks the long run can be 5 minutes shorter than an easy run (25 of 229 probed weeks), and a walk conversion or an easy step can land in a consolidation week so that total running does not fall (10 of 229); in low-volume starts the long run can be below the easy run in weeks 0-1. Non-blocking (R16).

Severity is ordinal only: compare Pareto first, then by leximax of the sorted severity multiset (worst first); counts or sums of costs are not used.

Any run, easy included, within sameSessionGapHours before MODERATE/HEAVY lower-body work carries a strength-axis cost when strength has a development role; no tie-break depends on candidate identifier strings; equal-harm opposing trade-offs under a JOINT lead are ASKed.

Quality-run-first may be the default for an equal-standing athlete only when the alternative places MODERATE/HEAVY lower-body work within nextDayGapHours before the key run; the choice is disclosed as a reversible population-based default, the athlete may choose otherwise, and repeated comparable athlete evidence may override it; for accustomed lifters the asymmetry is weaker and must be disclosed as such.

Unknown arrangement-level response is admissible only when current whole-week tolerance covers the same task set and frequency, the candidate's worst H0 severity is <= LOW, and it introduces no same-day pairing absent from the athlete's reported routine; otherwise it needs arrangement evidence or ASK; adverse arrangement evidence excludes it.
The trace names the decisive comparison (for example LOWEST_WORST_CASE_JOINT_HARM) whenever non-identical candidates were compared.
No universal spacing minimum; the gap bins rank options and never forbid a feasible arrangement by themselves.

Cold start: same-day pairings arising from the athlete's own chosen days and shifts are admissible and ranked; when the selected arrangement carries a MODERATE or higher H0 cost the program discloses it and offers the shift or day change as a negotiation option.

Near an event, arrangements follow days to the race: no strength in the last raceWeekStrengthMinDaysBeforeRace days; at most one short light session (raceWeekStrengthSets sets, main lifts, RIR >= raceWeekStrengthMinimumRir) on the strength day furthest from the race inside the race window; strength on taper days takes the taper dose.
limitations: Asymmetry evidence is acute and partly from unaccustomed lifters; chronic consequences of next-day arrangements are inferred.
Gap bins are operational.
Upper-body interaction claim relies on the local nature of interference, not a dedicated trial.

Operational values are reversible coaching choices inside the envelope, never physiological thresholds, injury-prevention rules, readiness scores, finish-time promises or individual-response predictions.
Steps advance only on executed comparable work without an adverse signal; nothing progresses from elapsed calendar time alone; completed history and official plan state stay immutable.

Interruption reasons are structured; any illness, injury, pain or clinical category, or a whole-word clinical-lexicon match in free text, routes CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED regardless of nonclinical or clinicalReason flags; an ambiguous or missing reason is ASK; the same rule applies to the intake pause and the legacy path.
Current eligibility must be assessed on or after the interruption end date.
SHORT (<= shortMaxDays): resume the last executed doses; the first quality slot runs easy; the next step waits for executed sessions.

MODERATE (<= moderateMaxDays): run entry from a current demonstration (modality RUN, easy/long/recovery-easy family, completed, conversational effort, compatible response, ordinary and next-day function, observed after the interruption began and within currentDemonstrationMaxAgeDays) or the reviewed 15-minute entry; at most moderateStepsToPrior conditional steps to the prior executed dose, each within the single-run ceiling of R6-PLANNED-PROGRESSION.

Strength return: every strength exposure of the return-entry week, including exercises first set up in it, is strengthEntrySets set(s) at RIR >= strengthEntryMinimumRir with the prior load only as a ceiling. Return step 2 is max(1, min(ceiling - 1, strengthEntrySets + 1)) sets at RIR 3, the ceiling being the last set count executed before the break outside a return step and outside a phase reduction (else the known count, else the normal count). Afterwards the count comes back at most one set per executed week without a phase reduction, up to the ceiling (a phase-reduced step 2 is followed by the step-2 count itself), and goes above it only through a later development block with no return-step exposure. Consolidation, specific, taper, race-week and post-event reductions apply on top, in the return steps too. Return-entry and return-step exposures never count toward a block-boundary set increase. During the return steps a logged load is capped at the current return reference (the load before the break until an entry log is adopted, then the adopted entry load) and asked about; the prior KNOWN load is prescribed only after a post-interruption logged entry load supports it, otherwise FROM_LOG from the entry log (D49; operational.return.strengthReturnSets, returnLoadCap).

LONG (> moderateMaxDays): restart class for running, with the achieved run peaks and the longest continuous run cleared so that taper, race-week, race-day and next-block doses and the race-day statement come only from runs executed after the restart (operational.return.restartRunHistory); strength re-establishes by effort; no prior-load KNOWN prescription until a post-interruption log exists.
EARNED is unavailable during RETURN/RESTART; surplus counts only observations after the return started.
No universal percentage rollback; historical maxima are ceilings, not current proof.

A nonclinical return requires a structured nonclinical reason category (legacy R5 contract: clinicalReason=false) and current eligibility assessed on or after the interruption end with every clinical flag false; free text can only add CLINICAL or ASK outcomes.

Interruption facts out of range or contradicting each other (days outside 1-3650 or not whole, unreal dates, start after end, dates after the review, days and dates disagreeing by more than one day) are asked, never resolved to the least conservative class; a clinical flag that means yes in any form routes to a human, one that is neither yes nor no is asked.
A run demonstration shorter than run.minimumSessionMinutes is not used as a demonstration.

Additions to the free-text screen (clinical terms, phrases, the damage-verb plus body-part rule) may only add CLINICAL or ASK outcomes; body parts alone stay ASK; a damage statement whose every damage verb is locally negated is ASK, never NONCLINICAL; a negation elsewhere in the clause never hides an affirmed damage statement.

A clinical eligibility flag that means yes in any form routes CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED in the intake, the review and the legacy path, as does a clinical status in any letter case; any other non-boolean flag leaves eligibility unassessed (ASK), never clearance and never assumed illness.
The round-8 lexical additions (R11) only add CLINICAL or ASK outcomes; 'Paternity leave' and 'Funeral and grief' stay nonclinical; conservative false positives are owned-gap residuals.

The return ends for every exercise: an exercise not used during the return steps carries no return step once the exercises in use complete theirs, and rotation resumes on its cadence afterwards. In use means prescribed in the week, executed or not: a missed in-use exposure keeps its exercise at its step and the return open, and a week without strength exposure ends nothing (D51, resolved in round 10; dossier Q2).

An exercise that reappears after a return without having been performed during it is established by effort when it was never performed (including one first prescribed in a session dated inside the pause) and re-established by effort when it was last performed more than return.moderateMaxDays earlier, counted from its last executed exposure (D52).
limitations: Direct evidence on nonclinical pause-length dosing is sparse; length classes are operational.
Cause verification relies on self-report.

The interruption-reason text screen is a lexicon heuristic; any further lexical residual is an owned open gap, and the structured category plus current eligibility (dated after the break, every clinical flag false) remain the primary defence.
Pregnancy and postpartum are excluded at intake by a structured field, but a review or return has no structured re-check; free text is the only backstop there (R11).
Phase-reduced weeks do not raise the return count, so a return across consolidation or taper weeks takes longer.
A block containing any return exposure earns no set: the boundary set can wait up to one more block (probe X: 3 sets through week 15 after a break in week 4).
Pregnancy and postpartum status is not asked again at reviews or returns (R11, second half; Product/Data).
A bodyweight exercise rotated back after a return resumes its earlier set count at RIR 3 without a re-establishment step (R17).

Operational values are reversible coaching choices inside the envelope, never physiological thresholds, injury-prevention rules, readiness scores, finish-time promises or individual-response predictions.
Steps advance only on executed comparable work without an adverse signal; nothing progresses from elapsed calendar time alone; completed history and official plan state stay immutable.

Supported events are 10K and half-marathon only; one taper week plus the race week, progressive: taper-week easy runs within taperWeekRunVolumeRange and the long run within taperWeekLongRunRange of the executed peak; taper quality total work minutes within taperQualityWorkRange; race-week easy runs within raceWeekRunVolumeRange; the policy states these are per-session fractions.

Frequency is maintained; intensity is maintained only through work already executed in build/specific weeks; a race-effort touch at the policy dose >= raceWeekTouchMinDaysBeforeRace days before the race requires R6-RUN-QUALITY and an executed comparable quality session; shakeout strides require executed strides; otherwise easy.

Strength stays at a reduced dose: taper sets about taperStrengthSetFraction of the preceding dose at RIR >= 3; race week one session of raceWeekStrengthSets at RIR >= raceWeekStrengthMinimumRir no later than raceWeekStrengthMinDaysBeforeRace days before the race; no new exercise, load increase or rotation.

Post-event: no running before postEventFirstRunMinDaysAfterRace days; runs optional and easy within postEventEasyMinutes; one light strength session; redevelopment (NEXT_BLOCK) requires an eligibility and function assessment dated after the race; redevelopment fractions are declared in the policy.
The legacy path uses the athlete's event kind and only policy-declared fractions.
No finish-time, readiness or peak-performance claim.

Event proximity counts days to the race (raceWindowDays 6; 7 taper days per taper week before the window): race-window sessions have no long run and no quality, an optional shakeout the day before, at most one race-effort touch on the run day closest to the race that is >= raceWeekTouchMinDaysBeforeRace days out, and short easy runs; taper-day sessions take taper doses whichever calendar week they fall in; post-race sessions follow the post-event rules by days since the race; a race date marked unavailable is asked about.
In WALK_JOG or RESTART mode, taper-day, race-window and post-event run sessions are reductions or holds of the achieved session of that mode, never a continuous run the mode has not reached (D43a).

Race day is a completion prescription at conversational effort with walk breaks (jog bouts no longer than achieved), without strides and without an instruction to press, when the race-week mode is WALK_JOG, RESTART or RETURN, when the athlete was in WALK_JOG or RESTART mode in any week of the program before the race (D47), or for a half marathon whose achieved long run is below raceDayCompletion.halfMarathonAchievedLongRunBelowMinutes; race-day warm-up strides and shakeout strides for any athlete only after executed strides (D43b-c, R9).

Whenever race day is a completion, the program or the proposal carries the non-blocking negotiation, recomputed from the race-week state of every proposal (added, replaced or removed), stating the longest continuous run executed by race week (never 0 when such a run was counted; a restart after a long interruption starts the count again), why race day is a completion, and both options (keep the event with walk breaks; a later or shorter event) (D43d, D47).
In taper weeks and at the start of the next block the long run is never shorter than that week's easy run (R10).
Walk/jog and restart steps do not advance on taper, race-window or post-event days; the next block resumes the walk/jog ladder one step back.
No exemption from the history-based completion applies unless it is declared and reviewed (D47c).
limitations: Taper evidence is from trained athletes; recreational evidence observational.
Combined run+strength taper evidence is indirect.
Post-event recovery evidence is from a simulated half-marathon.
The 6-day race window and the 7-day taper-day split are operational; completion with walk breaks is supported only indirectly (run/walk trial in marathoners, abstract only).
Which rebuilt long run, if any, should exempt a walk/jog- or restart-class athlete from the completion default is not established; no exemption applies until one is declared and reviewed.

The stated run counts runs in weeks whose gate advanced; after a restart applied in the last one or two weeks before the race it can read 'no continuous run yet' although restart runs were executed (R14).

dossierAnswers.question: Q1 (D50, a held week): when the share cap holds the long run and the easy run steps, the long run waits; that week the stepped easy session can equal the long run, never exceed it (60/35: E15/E15/L20 -> E20/E15/L20, then L25). Acceptable?
dossierAnswers.answer: Accepted. Probe S2: in 62 non-consolidation weeks the longest easy run equals the long run (mostly two 15-minute minimum sessions in weeks 1-2, some after a held week), and an easy run above the long run occurs only in a pre-existing week-1 split of 45-minute athletes (E25/L20), not after a held week. The one-increase rule holds against the 30-day reference in all 232 weeks whose long run steps beyond a sub-50-minute reference. Equality creates no single-session spike: the evidence relates injury to a session longer than the longest run of the previous 30 days (R6-S02), and the stepped easy session never exceeds the long run already prescribed. The athlete-facing "held within its share of the week until easy running grows" is accurate.

dossierAnswers.question: Q2 (D51, in use): "in use" means prescribed in the week, so a missed session never ends a return for its exercise; exercises not used during the return lose their markers only when those in use finish. Confirm.
dossierAnswers.answer: Confirmed, with one consequence that belongs to D52. Probe Y2: a missed squat in the step-2 week, all strength missed in the step-2 week, and all strength missed in the entry week each keep the return open until the exposure is executed, and a week without strength exposure ends nothing; 39 of 42 returns carry steps for three planned weeks because the entry week's first strength session is usually dated inside the pause. "Prescribed in the week" also covers that session, which cannot be executed: an exercise that first appears in it becomes established without a log and, once the clearing ends the return, comes back as a FROM_LOG row pointing to a log that does not exist (probe Z3). That is fixed by D52 (A), not by redefining "in use".

dossierAnswers.question: Q3 (R14): is R14 acceptable as an open gap tied to G03?
dossierAnswers.answer: Yes, as a non-blocking open gap for FREEZE-2. Probe V still shows it (a restart applied in the last two weeks before the race; the item states 0 although a 15-minute restart run was executed), and race day remains a completion there, so no dose is affected. It understates executed running in an athlete-facing statement, so it must be closed before any use beyond the offline reference, together with the Product/Data classification of sessions dated inside a declared pause.

dossierAnswers.question: Q4 (consolidation long run): in a consolidation week the long run can fall 5 minutes below an easy run (4 of 207 weeks before D50, 18 after). Required before freeze (policy change and full review) or a non-blocking recommendation?
dossierAnswers.answer: A non-blocking recommendation for the next policy revision (R16). My probe S2 reproduces the effect on a larger grid: 25 of 229 consolidation weeks with a long run (5 of 229 with the reconstructed round-9 r6-program.mjs), always by 5 minutes. In all 229 the week's longest run is at or below the previous week's, so there is no single-session spike (R6-S02); total running falls in 219 of 229 (220 on the round-9 runtime). The exceptions predate D50: a walk conversion or an easy step planned into the consolidation week. A deload is a reduction of overall training stress (R6-S44, R6-S45); no study addresses how a reduced running week is distributed across sessions (negative search r10recoveryweek). The inversion is a coherence issue, not a sporting risk, and fixing it needs policy text. R16: in the next revision, keep the long run at least as long as the week's easy runs in consolidation weeks and in the first cold-start weeks (extending the R10 floor), and plan no new easy level and no walk conversion into a consolidation week, so its total running falls; with a full delta review.

dossierAnswers.question: Binding defects D50 and D51 (round 9)
dossierAnswers.answer: D50 resolved: probe S (round-9 grid, unchanged) 0 of 66 programs with 4 or more consecutive flat build weeks (round 9: 47), 0 with 6 or more (42), 9 whose internal easy minutes never change (35; all four-run-day athletes stepping one easy run at a time, longest flat run 1-2 weeks); probe S2 0 one-increase violations, the quality ladder advances (90/40: 0 -> 7 steps), executed programs keep growing. D51 resolved: probes Y and Y2, returns end with the exercises in use, rotation resumes on its calendar cadence in all 25 rotating timelines with weeks left, nothing later gets the return-entry dose, and no block in progress at the break earns a set; on the reconstructed round-9 runtime the same returns never end.

dossierAnswers.question: New binding defect found in round 10
dossierAnswers.answer: D52 (load establishment, shared with substitution, rotation and the return): the strength state is updated from prescriptions rather than executions. A missed first establishment exposure leaves the exercise established without a log, so its next row says "Use the load you logged last time for this exercise" with the full set count and a progression rule (probe Z: rotation, cold start, an equipment-window substitute, after a return); and the 28-day re-establishment clock counts the last prescribed week, so a back squat skipped for five weeks resumes at 4x5 at the prior 82.5 kg after 42 days, and the gap is unbounded. It predates FREEZE-1; D51 makes it reachable after a return; I did not detect it in rounds 1 to 9. The fix is runtime-only.
